Single-open-card cap verified: this is the only open console-bump card (predecessors all closed). Type intent: **Task** (`type` field not set — `list_issue_types` 403 for this credential).

**`target:v17`** (class ① + ④, same grading as #6813): the gap holds a shipped fix (objectui#4298) the build refuses to serve — already cost one retest a false "still broken" verdict — and #7804's authorable key is unusable through the Studio designer (dashboards carrying it become unopenable-for-editing), so an RC cut with this pin ships both.

Dispatch constraints: ⛔ pin bump is never a rider — dedicated bump script with override + lockfile; the dev re-reads the actual objectui range at claim time (405-commit figure goes stale hourly). The **staleness-gate suggestion in the body is out of scope** for this card — if pursued it is a separate card, and note it would be a new CI gate (maintainer-floor for gate additions/weakening applies to its design).

Size/model suggestion: S mechanical, `sonnet` — the bump script + rebuild + the two named re-checks.

## ⚠️ Correction to the card, and it changes the shape of the work

The card closes with: *"a gate that fails when the pin falls more than N commits or M days behind would have caught both of these before QA did — right now the only signal is `scripts/check-console-sha.mjs`, which verifies dist matches the pin and says nothing about whether the pin matches reality."*

**That gate already exists, it is already red, and it already prescribes the fix.** Measured just now:

```
$ node scripts/check-objectui-pin-fresh.mjs      → EXIT=1
  ::error::objectui pin is stale — refresh .objectui-sha before releasing (#3340).
  Fix — move the pin, then let the Version Packages PR rebuild:
      scripts/bump-objectui.sh
      node scripts/objectui-range.mjs <old> <new>
```

It even distinguishes itself from the gate the card names: *"This is NOT ci.yml's 'Console Pin Gate' (#4290). That gate proves the pinned SHA still BUILDS; this one proves the pin is still CURRENT. Either can be green while the other is red."*

**And its absence from the RC cut is deliberate, not a hole** — `.github/workflows/cut-rc.yml` carries a header section titled *"WHY NOT `check:objectui-pin-fresh` HERE (and why that is not a hole)"*, because it enforces on the **GA** cut. So the answer to "why didn't a gate catch this" is: the gate exists and fires at GA, and this pin went stale between RC cuts. ⇒ **⛔ Do not build a second staleness gate on this card.** If a *threshold* change is wanted, that is its own card with its own argument.

## Release-boundary note

`bump-objectui.sh` writes a changeset and the Version Packages PR later rebuilds from it. Bumping the pin and committing the changeset is **ordinary work**. ⛔ **Merging a Version Packages PR, publishing, or tagging is a release action and is forbidden to every AI seat** (#6170) — that boundary is stated in the dispatch so it cannot be crossed by momentum.

## ⚠️ My dispatch assumption was wrong, and the dev corrected it

I wrote in Block 2: *"objectui `origin/main` is now `6d77acf`, past the `b4d3c2204` the card measured ⇒ **the gap is bigger than 405**."*

**The gap is 123, and it was never 405.** Three independent measurements agree — `rev-list` 123, `--first-parent` 123, and `check:objectui-pin-fresh`'s own log-walk reporting "123 non-merge commit(s)" — and the card's own waypoint is arithmetically consistent with it (`OLD..b4d3c2204` = 121, `b4d3c2204..HEAD` = 2, and `b4d3c2204` is an ancestor of the new pin). So the pin was **121 behind at filing**, and the card's "an order of magnitude larger than #7411's 18" framing rested on an unreproducible number. I inherited that number and made it worse by asserting a direction on top of it.

**I could not independently reproduce the count from the PM seat** — this container's objectui checkout is shallow and does not contain the old pin, which is the exact limitation `check:objectui-pin-fresh` warns about in its own output. So I am accepting three internally-consistent measurements plus the waypoint arithmetic, and saying so rather than implying I re-derived it.

## The two symptoms got separate verdicts, which is what the card needed

**Symptom 1 — FIXED, and confirmed at three levels rather than assumed:** the fixing commit is in range (`3c6e84cca`); the card's own probe returns `combo: 'combo'` at the new pin and returned nothing at the old; and **the rebuilt bundle actually serves it** — `assets/plugin-dashboard-sS6Qwuba.js` carries the resolved `…sankey:sankey,combo:combo}`. Checking the artifact, not just the source, is the step that makes this a real verdict.

**Symptom 2 — NOT FIXED, and no pin bump can fix it.** The console vendors the **published** `@objectstack/spec`, pinned `^17.0.0-rc.6` at both the old and new objectui pin. npm's `17.0.0-rc.6` was published 2026-08-10T13:09Z; #7804's key landed 2026-08-12T11:36Z — **two days later**. And `17.0.0-rc.6` is simultaneously the highest version on npm *and* this repo's own `packages/spec/package.json` version, so **the workspace has moved past the published tarball under an unchanged version string** and even the `^` range cannot reach the new content. Verified against the tarball actually installed into the build tree: zero matches.

The probe deserves note too — a bare grep for `object` false-positives on `optionsFrom.object`, so it probed #7804's own `describe()` text instead. Same discipline this lane has been re-learning all day.

**Filed as #8134**, and generalised correctly: *any* authorable key added to `packages/spec` after the last spec publish is server-accepted and round-trips, while the Studio designer rejects it as unrecognized — and the framework-side card closes **green**, because `packages/spec`'s own pins pass. Fixing it needs a spec release → an objectui relock → another pin bump: three ordered steps across two repos. `#8134 remains open`.

## The baseline green was vacuous, and it said so

`check:console-sha` exited **0 before the bump** — but on *"No console dist at `packages/console/dist` — skipping SHA check."* A gate that skips when its subject is absent and reports success is the same failure family as #8024's dead self-test, and it was sitting green under this card the whole time. Worth remembering the next time that gate is cited as evidence.

## The ADR-0087 judgment call — I checked the load-bearing claim myself

`bump-objectui.sh` emitted an `adr-0087: TODO` placeholder that the registration gate rejects by design (10 breaking changes in range). The dev judged the ten individually and answered `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. That is a governance answer on ten breaking changes, so I verified the argument it rests on rather than accepting the conclusion:

```
packages/console/package.json
  files:   ['dist', 'README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md']
  exports: {"./package.json": "./package.json"}
  main / types: none
  @object-ui/* runtime deps: NONE
```

**Confirmed.** `@objectstack/console` publishes a frozen prebuilt SPA whose sole export is its own `package.json`; it forwards no `@object-ui/*` entry point and re-exports none of those types, so the ten breaking TypeScript declaration surfaces are unreachable through it. And no `packages/spec` schema, authorable key or protocol surface moved in range, so there is no stored-metadata rewrite for `objectstack migrate meta` to prescribe. The judgment holds **on mechanism**, not on assertion.

## The changeset is a release-record artifact in its own right

99 releasing of 115 changesets across the 123 commits, each breaking entry individually marked, and — the part that matters — the **11 commits carrying no changeset are listed by subject rather than counted**, with the reason stated: *"a count cannot tell a dependency bump from a form-behaviour change."* That is the difference between a release record that looks complete and one that is.

Marking ready and arming auto-merge. Tracked to MERGED with the `closed_by_pull_requests` check.
